name: Charter Day
description: Charter Day, observed on the second Monday of February, is a mandatory paid holiday across all corponation employment contracts in M88, established by the 2210 Meridian Compact — a multi-corponation agreement that standardized worker observance days as a concession to labor unrest following the 2209 BCI Workers' Strike. Officially, it 'celebrates the founding principles of cooperative enterprise between corponation and citizen.' In practice, it is universally understood as a purchased peace offering, and most workers spend it either nursing genuine grievances or participating in the city's largest unofficial drinking and street culture event, which has organically grown around the mandated day off.
cultural_impact: Charter Day has the highest single-day street market revenue of any date on the M88 calendar, because the corponations mandated a holiday but couldn't mandate how people spend it — the Shelf runs its largest ghost markets of the year while corporate plazas run 'Compact Celebration' events that almost no one attends.
key_figures: Director Cassian Mbeki-Holst (Aurelius, primary Compact signatory)
The Shelf DJ collective 'Compact Disc' (named satirically)
locations: Meridian Compact Plaza, MidRing (official; usually empty)
The Grand Sprawl ghost market, Shelf Ward 11 (unofficial; massive)
Spire Level 40 — private Charter galas for Tier 5 executives
story_hooks: The 2209 BCI Workers' Strike had a secret clause buried in the Compact settlement — and someone has found it, and it's due to activate on the next Charter Day.
The Compact Disc collective has obtained a broadcast license for Charter Day and plans to transmit from the Shelf into Tier 3-4 frequencies — the corponations want the signal stopped before it airs.

A player character is a corporate security contractor assigned to keep the Charter Day ghost market 'within acceptable parameters' — a job that gets complicated when they realize they grew up on the Shelf.
origin_event: The 2210 Meridian Compact, a multi-corponation labor agreement signed as a direct concession following the 2209 BCI Workers' Strike, which shut down 40% of M88's networked infrastructure for 19 days.
tier_observations: Tier 1 (Shelf): The Grand Sprawl ghost market; street parties; Compact Disc broadcasts; genuine celebration of the day off even while mocking what it represents — the holiday belongs to the Shelf culturally. Tier 2: Mixed — some join Shelf markets, some stay home, some attend corponation 'appreciation events' for the catered food. Tier 3: Brunch culture, ironic Charter Day toasts, some genuine enjoyment. Tier 4: Mandatory attendance at company Charter galas with performance reviews pending afterward; the 'celebration' is a pressure event. Tier 5 (Spire): Private galas, genuine congratulatory atmosphere among the executives who negotiated the Compact — they consider it a victory of managed concession.
